payload.blocks: Phase 9 of plan 261122-1946 (AGENTS.md cut) and phase 11's byte numbers; phases 8 and 10 go on meanwhile.
payload.headline: Phase 9: workers get no composed rules, so cutting AGENTS.md would strip their rules

parts.cause: The spec has the worker prompt adapter supply worker facts (role, domain, stage), but the PromptPort trait carries only a persona name, and decision ASC-D1 says PromptPort does not change. Phase 5 therefore moved only the persona block. The rule units are all scope repo, so the cut changes only this repo's AGENTS.md.

options.cost: About half a day of agent work; phase 9 waits for it.
options.does: Add a PromptPort seam that passes the worker's facts and places the matched rules in its prompt (amends ASC-D1), then cut AGENTS.md as the phase lists.
options.gain: The full byte cut; each worker gets exactly the rules its facts match.
options.harm: Changes the execution prompt contract and its vectors; every worker prompt grows by the rules it now reads from AGENTS.md.
options.label: A: workers compose rules too

options.cost: Small: the when: lines and the anchor tests.
options.does: Cut only what workers never need (dispatch, capability routing, run door, driver discipline, domain doctrine read, gateway, convention paths); keep the code-change rules in AGENTS.md.
options.gain: No contract change; nothing is lost for any session; done today.
options.harm: A smaller cut, roughly half of what the phase hoped for.
options.label: B: keep worker rules standing

options.does: Close the plan without phase 9 and open it as its own item later.
options.harm: AGENTS.md stays as large as today.
options.label: C: defer phase 9

parts.recommendation: B. The cut only affects this repo's own AGENTS.md (mission boundary: little gain for other projects), and B keeps every worker's rules without touching the execution contract. A can follow later as its own item if the bytes matter.

scope.allows: Which rules phase 9 cuts, and whether PromptPort may change for it.
scope.forbids: Any change to which rules exist or what they say.

parts.what: Phase 9 moves rules such as before-touching-code, definition-of-done, design-principles, RUL11 and RUL104 out of AGENTS.md, to reach agents only through compose at start. Heads get them that way, and hand-opened Claude sessions will after phase 10. Worker prompts do not: their start takes only the persona block from the composer, so a worker would lose those rules entirely.
